scope: Proposition 6.17 (Relative collar comparison) of the manuscript “Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one” (preprints/Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bf15a86507a10184), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 95. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider two finite positive FK laws at the fixed q, with ordinary collar bonds, whose graphs and deterministic wires agree on the remote side of a sequence of regular collars and whose unknown-side data are permitted in the sense of Definition 6.12. Require each collar to have one of the following geometries: (i) a full annulus with no named bank hubs, or one sector whose only bank attachments are continuous primal wire portions along its two side rays, crossing the collar and each met by its primal wall-to-wall screen; (ii) two sectors, with only such screen-met continuous primal wire portions on both side rays of one sector, no bank or hub attachment in the other, and no direct contact between the sectors inside the collar. Side graphs may join contacts of the two sectors only through the corresponding permitted radial cap. After m further collars of a sufficiently large fixed ratio and one final comparison collar, the expectations of any fixed nonnegative function f supported beyond them satisfy, for fixed C ≥ 1 and 0 < c < 1, the two inequalities E1f ≤  1 + (C − 1)(1 − c)m E2f, E2f ≤  1 + (C − 1)(1 − c)m E1f. (6.21) They are understood in the extended nonnegative reals. For finite positive expectations they imply E1f/E2f = 1 + O((1 − c)m), and the expectations vanish together. The constants are independent of the far graph, the unknown-side partition, and f. The same conclusion holds in the reverse radial direction and after a positive finite tilt supported on the unknown side. In particular, unknown-side changes may join or separate the designated wire portions. The contraction requires the enumerated screen-met attachments; the general bound on J in Definition 6.12 alone is not sufficient for it.
